doc.title: Marty Morell interviewed by Monk Rowe, Orlando, Florida, February 24, 2017

title: Getting fired by Marian McPartland
summary: Too adventurous a young drummer, he was replaced while playing with Steve Kuhn and Ron Carter.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: And I see you played with Marian McPartland somewhere along the way.

Yeah, yeah, back in the day, yeah I played with her. But what happened with Marian, that was during the time I was playing with Steve Kuhn and we had just done an album with Gary McFarland, a thing called “October Suite.” Ron Carter was the bass player. And I was working with Marian. And I had to take a couple of nights off and I sent in a friend of mine to sub for me, right? A guy named Jimmy Capas. And then on the next gig he was on, so I got axed by Marian. But I think what happened was that I was maybe trying to stretch out a little bit too much. She wanted more mainstream, just a little more solid kind of, you know and I was young and a little bit cocky and I tried to push her a little bit.
What was that thing Lester Young said —
Where she didn’t want to go.
Some quote from Lester Young, “Just tickety-tick for Lester, don’t be dropping no bombs” or something. © Fillius Jazz Archive -16-

Yeah. I guess I got a little too adventurous. But she was really sweet. She sent me some sheet music, some tunes that I liked, and that’s fine. Sometimes it just doesn’t work out. And it didn’t really bother me. Because I was playing with Steve Kuhn and Ron Carter.
Yeah, that was some nice music.
